_rule: One story per experiment followers can watch. status: getting ready | running | on hold | result. Every update is dated and links to its record. The generator writes the block into README.md and FOLLOW.md; status_check refuses a stale or unchecked board. Plain words, American English, no claims beyond the record.

stories.headline: Building a bigger map of healthy cells: IAM-Atlas v2.1
stories.why: Every IAM reading compares a sample with healthy cells. The atlas is that comparison: a map of what 74 kinds of healthy human cells look like. Version 2.1 more than doubles the samples behind it and adds second and third laboratories for key cells, so the map stops depending on any one lab's habits.
stories.hope: The new laboratories agree with the old ones, the map gets steadier, and tests that were too close to call, like lung, get a fair chance.
stories.risk: Cells grown in a dish may have drifted too far to use; a new laboratory may disagree with the old ones; the fit may need more computing time than planned.

updates.text: Version 2 published with its own DOI, so anyone can download the map and check it.
The plan is locked before any new data is opened: which samples build the map and which are kept back to test it.
First step running: measuring how much growing cells in a dish changes them.

Culture check, first result: growing cells in a dish changes them a lot. In the cleanest comparison, about 1 in 9 of the sites we read moves steadily as the cells keep dividing. Those sites will be set aside before any dish-grown cell is compared with the atlas. Two more laboratories' data are next.

stories.headline: Does our second instrument read the same DNA the same way everywhere?
stories.why: Before anyone trusts an instrument, it has to give the same answer on the same sample. We read identical reference DNA prepared with five different kits in two laboratories.
stories.hope: The one check that failed turns out to come from how we sampled three very large files, not from the laboratories.
stories.risk: If the difference is real, that kit's lab-to-lab check stays failed and the record says so.

updates.text: Four of five checks passed: repeats agree, kits agree, and a planted change was seen every time. The lab-to-lab check failed on three files, so by our own rule nothing is declared until the cause is found.
The cause test is written and listed in the run ledger. It starts when rented-computer prices and availability allow.
